look_here_first: Follow a trailing stem to a node: opposite petiolate, toothed leaves and stems that can root at the nodes. Then inspect a long-stalked solitary head: the disk becomes a conspicuous elongated conical receptacle with chaffy paleae as fruits mature. Confirm with mature compressed dark cypselae; ray color alone is weak.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Creeping to sprawling perennial herb in moist or disturbed ground; lower stem nodes may root.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Opposite petiolate leaves, usually lanceolate to ovate, serrate; upper leaves may vary in position.

key_traits.label: Heads
key_traits.text: Solitary pedunculate composite heads with small yellowish rays and disk; receptacle elongates to a cone with persistent chaffy paleae in fruit.

key_traits.label: Fruits
key_traits.text: Compressed dark cypselae about 1–2.5 mm; pappus generally absent. Look for fruiting cone and paleae.

key_traits.label: Best field traits
key_traits.text: opposite toothed petiolate leaves at rooting nodes; long-stalked solitary heads; conical chaffy receptacle in fruit; small dark cypselae usually without pappus

lookalikes.differences: Eclipta prostrata also has opposite leaves and wet-ground habit, but usually has small white rays and different fruit/head architecture. Synedrella nodiflora bears small axillary or terminal heads and a more erect habit; compare ray/cypsela morphology. Sphagneticola trilobata often has 3-lobed leaves and much larger showy rays. Confirm the elongated chaffy receptacle and fruit, not just leaf arrangement.
